fixed_before.latest_successor: exact spectral-variance Hessian defect, effective gap, and three-dyadic-block state rigidity

new_theorem.name: NM10-AVP3-JOINT-HESSIAN-SLACK-16
new_theorem.summary: The sharp Bellman envelope has an exact nonnegative joint state-input slack Sigma_p. It decomposes into the prior state spectral-variance defect, an input-direction Hessian defect, and a Hessian Cauchy/alignment defect. Sigma_p enters Ito as additional coercivity and gives a strictly stronger data-dependent endpoint extrapolation bound than the state-only kappa_p refinement.
new_theorem.near_sharp_stability: if R_p(Y)>=q R_p^*, then sigma_p <= 2 delta(q^{-2}-1); if q=1-eps>=1/2 then sigma_p<=12 eps delta
new_theorem.cross_alignment: for p>=5/2 and q>=1/2, the integrated cross-Hessian saturation ratio chi_p obeys 1-chi_p <=1.41(q^{-2}-1)
new_theorem.extremal_cone: At an exact eigenspace state Az=a^2 z, Sigma_p has a closed shell formula and vanishes iff Y=gamma Z with gamma>=0. Globally Sigma_p=0 iff Z lies in one eigenspace and Y is a nonnegative scalar multiple of Z.

source_level_movement: none: strong endpoint and full critical exponent bracket unchanged
demonstrated_mechanism_gain: Any branch that could beat the critical 2/3 scale must now annihilate the full Bellman slack, not merely the state spectral variance. Near-sharp subcritical responses simultaneously concentrate into a narrow spectral packet and saturate the positive state-input Hessian alignment; exact shell migration forcing away from the current state direction pays an explicit linear-plus-quadratic slack. This identifies the sharp cone underlying the one-shell feedback obstruction and gives a coercive quantity for an active packet-migration Carleson argument.
failed_or_nonclosing_routes: The state-only spectral-variance defect cannot close the endpoint because one-shell states have zero state defect.

The new joint slack still does not by itself control a state that is only approximately, rather than exactly, in a moving three-block packet; a robust packet-level lower bound for Sigma_p is the remaining bridge.
next_attack: Prove an approximate packet migration inequality: when Z has small leakage outside a three-adjacent-dyadic packet, lower-bound Sigma_p by a weighted amount of forcing outside that packet plus an error controlled by the state leakage. Combine with the prior packet-rigidity and Hellinger/decoherence estimates to obtain a summable active migration charge.
